title: Migration Amendment (Putting Local Workers First) Bill 2016
short_title: Migration Amendment (Putting Local Workers First) Bill 2016

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change the Migration Act 1958 to alter the temporary work visa system.
It would require employers to meet stronger labour market testing and a new Australian Jobs Test before sponsoring temporary skilled workers.
Sponsors in certain sectors with more than a set proportion of 457 visa holders would have to use a Labour Agreement instead of standard sponsorship.
changes: Strengthen labour market testing for employers nominating 457 visa workers.
Introduce an Australian Jobs Test that employers must pass to sponsor temporary workers.
Require sponsors in specified sectors with a high proportion of 457 visa holders to use a Labour Agreement.
summary.affected: Employers who sponsor temporary skilled workers and Australian workers.

speeches.speaker: Bill Shorten
speeches.brief: The Migration Amendment (Putting Local Workers First) Bill 2016 proposed tighter 457 visa rules, including mandatory four-week job advertising, a ban on ads excluding local workers, and a new ‘Australian jobs test’ for labour agreements. It cited 700,000 unemployed Australians and a 130,000 drop in apprenticeships, and required licensed trade visa holders to hold an Australian licence or pass a skills assessment, referencing exploitation at Pizza Hut, 7-Eleven and Caltex.
